voice.stance: The spoken voice. OBEYA text is read at three meters, in a morning stand-up, by people wearing gloves. Write the way a good site lead talks: names, numbers, today. A line that cannot be said out loud to the person it concerns does not go on the wall.
voice.title_grammar: A real question the meeting has to answer, or a call to act.
voice.title_example: Who unblocks the north loops this week?

do.why: Ownership is the law of this language, and a name on a wall gets acted on.

do.rule: Keep the time words at today and this week.
do.why: The board resets daily. Anything older belongs in SAGA.
Nobody reads a paragraph standing up.

dont.why: The stand-up is about the next 24 hours.

dont.rule: No abbreviations that need decoding at distance.
dont.why: At three meters an abbreviation is wallpaper.

dont.rule: Never write a count you have not counted.
dont.why: "Several items" and "various stakeholders" name nothing and get assigned to nobody.

contrast.generic: There are several outstanding items requiring attention from various stakeholders across the project.
contrast.voiced: Three blockers today. Crane permit: Nadia. Cable drums: contractor. Scaffold: Sam, Thursday.
